connections.observation: σωφροσύνη is introduced (s001) as rule over pleasures of πότοι, ἀφροδίσια, ἐδωδαί (s004); the concrete cluster then unfolds in the quoted scenes — Odyssean feast, Zeus overcome by ἀφροδισίων ἐπιθυμίαν — where the counter-example καρτερίαι/τέτλαθι (s010) is set beside ἐπιλανθανόμενον and ἐκπλαγέντα. The abstract term at 389d and its opposite enactments in cited verse stand in the same section.

σωφρονεστάτου applied to Peleus (s001) is placed immediately beside the diagnosis of Achilles as containing νοσήματε δύο ἐναντίω ἀλλήλοιν (s014): the superlative of the section's opening virtue names the father just as the son is charged with its two contraries.

The dense δῶρον concentration at 390e with δωροδόκους and φιλοχρημάτους (s002) returns compressed inside Achilles' first disease, ἀνελευθερίαν μετὰ φιλοχρηματίας (s014); the earlier lexical density reappears as one half of the paired νοσήματε.

Forms of πείθω (s003), the -τέον verbal adjectives including πειστέον and ἀκουστέον (s008), and the recurrences of ἀκούω (s016) are woven together: what the young ἀκούουσιν and what is πειστέον are governed by the same prescriptive verbal-adjective series, and πείθω itself appears both as Homeric ἐπιπείθεο and as πεισθείς describing the harmed listener.

The μέν/δέ contrast of ἀρχόντων ὑπηκόους / ἄρχοντας ἡδονῶν (s005) is completed by νεανιεύματα ἰδιωτῶν εἰς ἄρχοντας, placing νεανίαι (s007) on both sides: those who must obey rulers and rule themselves are the same young whose insolent speech toward rulers is then quoted.

The accumulated articulations of divine parentage — θεᾶς παῖς, θεοῦ παῖδα, θεῶν ἀγχίσποροι, αἷμα δαιμόνων (s009) — sit inside the enumeration θεῶν, δαιμόνων, ἡρώων, ἐν Ἅιδου, ἀνθρώπων (s011); the heroes-as-god-children discussion at 391c–e occupies exactly the δαιμόνων/ἡρώων slot the enumeration then names as completed.

The descending sequence gods→daimons→heroes→Hades→humans (s011) halts at ἀνθρώπων with ἀδύνατον … ἐν τῷ παρόντι τάξαι (s012); the poets' paired contrasts ἄδικοι εὐδαίμονες / δίκαιοι ἄθλιοι and ἀλλότριον ἀγαθόν / οἰκεία ζημία (s013) are cited as the very content whose refutation must wait for δικαιοσύνη to be found.

The quoted line δῶρα θεοὺς πείθει, δῶρʼ αἰδοίους βασιλῆας joins the δῶρον density (s002) to the πείθω recurrence (s003) at a single point: gifts persuading gods stands at 390e as the hinge from which the subsequent chain of πείθεσθαι/πειστέον/πειθώμεθα about the young unfolds.

new_signals.observation: The superlative σοφώτατος appears twice: of the wisest man (Odysseus) whose speech about full tables is quoted, and of Chiron as Achilles' wisest educator.

elements.context: ἐπιτήδειον εἶναι πρὸς ἐγκράτειαν ἑαυτοῦ ἀκούειν νέῳ

new_signals.observation: ἐπιτήδειος recurs three times as the criterion by which cited verses are judged suitable or unsuitable for the young to hear.

elements.context: οὐδʼ ὅσιον ταῦτά γε κατὰ Ἀχιλλέως φάναι

new_signals.observation: ὅσιος recurs paired with ἀληθῆ, marking the twofold ground on which the stories are rejected.
